system.name: Cygnus X-1
system.description: One of the first stellar black hole candidates ever identified, 7,240 light-years away. It feeds on mass stripped from its blue supergiant companion HDE 226868, shining brilliantly in X-rays as matter spirals into the accretion disk.

cygnusx1-bh.name: Cygnus X-1
cygnusx1-bh.description: A stellar-mass black hole of about 21 solar masses, formed when a massive star collapsed. It accretes material from the wind of its companion star, generating intense X-ray emission that was first detected in 1964 — making it one of the earliest black hole candidates ever found.
cygnusx1-bh.funFact: In 1974, Stephen Hawking bet Kip Thorne that Cygnus X-1 was NOT a black hole — he conceded the bet in 1990 once the evidence became overwhelming.

hde226868.name: HDE 226868
hde226868.description: A luminous O9.7 Iab blue supergiant and one of the brightest stars in the sky. Its powerful stellar wind feeds a constant stream of gas onto the Cygnus X-1 black hole. Despite being roughly twice as massive as the black hole, the star is slowly being cannibalized by its dark companion.
hde226868.funFact: HDE 226868 is so luminous it would outshine every star visible to the naked eye if placed at the same distance as Alpha Centauri.
